tests.testName: every build and debug prompt that runs tests carries local-pre-commit
local-pre-commit covers test runs made while working, not only before a commit

challengeFindings.title: Ship Step 2 on the MCP path (exit 80) treats a PR whose only non-green check was cancelled as green and moves on, while the gh path stops on the same rollup

bkit-debug-failure-reproduce runs tests while it works ("with the repo's test runner and a file or name filter", a name filter alone collects the whole suite) but does not carry local-pre-commit, and the new carrier test cannot see it because it only looks for bkit:test:file or bkit tests changed

Three prompts now carry two rules that contradict each other while working: Local tests first says "Exhaust the local test suite", and the new Local pre-commit says never run the full suite while working

A beforeAll / afterAll (or each-hook) given its own longer timeout, such as beforeAll(fn, 120_000), has every synchronous child call without a timeout killed at the file's hookTimeout (10 s unit, 30 s integration under CI), so a slow fixture build that used to pass now fails
An audit report that quotes a leaked token lands on `dev` under a `[skip ci]` head, so no CI workflow (incl. the `bkit-trivy` secret scan) runs on that push

tests.testName: Step 2's exit-80 arm stops on a cancelled, action-required or stale check without naming /bkit-debug
every debug prompt that runs tests by file or name filter carries local-pre-commit
local-tests-first does not ask for the full local suite that local-pre-commit forbids while working

challengeFindings.title: On the MCP path (exit 80) a PR whose only non-green check timed out, hit a startup failure or reports a commit status of `error` matches none of the stop arms and falls to Else → next sub-step as green, while the gh path counts the same check as failed

bkit-debug-failure-reproduce now carries Local pre-commit, but its step 6 still allows "a file or name filter" with the raw test runner and its PASS mapping asks it to show "other tests are unaffected", so the agent runs a name filter alone or a wider suite (the whole suite collected) with no named command to excuse it

The reworded Local tests first says "the full suite runs only in the pre-push hook" with no exception, so it contradicts the named full-suite runs of the steps that carry it (the `--fallback=bkit:gate:static-unit` of gaps-remediate and verify, the build group gate) and the Local pre-push arm for a repo without the hook, and an agent that follows it skips the run

On a stack whose test runner runs tests by package or folder and not by file (for example `go test ./internal/foo/`), the new Local pre-commit allows no valid run: it requires naming each test file and forbids a folder, so the agent either breaks the rule or skips the tests

On the MCP path (exit 80) ship Step 2 reads `pull_request_read` `get_status`, the combined commit status, which carries no GitHub Actions check runs and no cancelled, action-required or stale state, so a PR whose `bkit-trivy` secret scan was cancelled, awaits approval or failed reaches Step 3 when any other commit status is green

The new accepted-risk paragraph records that an audit report may reach `main` unscanned under a `[skip ci]` head, but the owner's decision accepted `dev` only, so a direct audit-only push to an unprotected consumer `main` skips every workflow with no recorded acceptance

tests.testName: Step 2's exit-80 arm continues only when every check passed and sends a timed-out, startup-failure or error check to /bkit-debug
bkit-debug-failure-reproduce runs its tests by naming each test file and asks for no unnamed wider run
Step 2's exit-80 arm reads check-run conclusions, not the combined commit status
